fr.recommendations:
Based on the aerial observations provided, here are the responder-safety recommendations:

• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.

• Mark each structure with a clearly visible identifier (e.g., "Main House," "Building 2," "Building 3") to help responders locate and communicate about specific structures quickly.

• Post a property map at the driveway entrance showing the locations of all structures, parking areas, access points, and the equipment and storage areas.

• Clear vegetation along the access drive to maintain a minimum width sufficient for emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.

• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive to maintain overhead clearance for fire apparatus and ladder trucks.

• Identify and mark a designated turnaround area for emergency vehicles near the structures, and keep it clear of parked vehicles and equipment at all times.

• Keep all secondary access points unlocked or secured only with a lockbox to allow responders to reach all sides of all structures.

• Clear a walking path between the main residence and both detached structures so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.

• Keep the equipment storage area and storage area free of materials that block vehicle or foot access to the surrounding structures.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs and grass that are growing directly next to the house to create open ground around the foundation.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Mow or cut grass across the open areas surrounding the house, particularly during dry months when it dries out and becomes more flammable.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material that has accumulated against or under shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Maintain the open separation already present between vegetation and the structure by cutting back any shrubs or trees that begin to close that gap over time.
• Clear grass and loose plant material from along the edges of the driveway to keep a clear path to and from the property.
